# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan: 5 Days, 2 Adults

A relaxed Kyoto itinerary for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14** that keeps each day under **12 km walking**, mixes temples, local food, and one museum-focused day, and stays within your **$1,800 total budget excluding flights**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

| Day | Focus | Walking | Transit | Estimated Cost for 2 |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Apr 10 | Higashiyama temples + old streets | 7–9 km | Subway + short bus / taxi hops | $180 |
| Apr 11 | Arashiyama nature + riverside temples | 8–10 km | JR train + local bus | $210 |
| Apr 12 | Museum day + central Kyoto food lanes | 5–7 km | Subway + walk | $170 |
| Apr 13 | Northern Kyoto temples + quiet neighborhoods | 6–9 km | Bus + taxi backup | $190 |
| Apr 14 | Fushimi sake district + departure-friendly day | 5–8 km | JR train + subway | $160 |

## 5-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start at **Kiyomizu-dera**, then stroll downhill through **Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka** at an easy pace.
- Afternoon: Visit **Yasaka Shrine** and **Maruyama Park**; keep the rest of the day unhurried with tea or dessert stops.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Yasaka Shrine** and **Maruyama Park**; keep the rest of the day unhurried with tea or dessert stops, Kyoto, Japan
- Food: Try **yudofu**, matcha sweets, and a simple soba lunch near Higashiyama.
- Rainy-day backup: **Kyoto National Museum** for indoor cultural time.
- Transit suggestion: Use **bus + taxi hops** between temple clusters to protect your walking limit.
- Estimated cost: Temple entries, transit, snacks, lunch, and dinner: **$180 total**.

### Day 2: Arashiyama and the River
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Take the **JR Sagano Line** to Arashiyama and walk the **Bamboo Grove** early before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Visit **Tenryu-ji** and then enjoy the river area with a slow café break or boat-side stroll.
- Food: Plan for **tofu dishes**, grilled skewers, and a dessert stop near the station area.
- Rainy-day backup: **Saga-Arashiyama area temples and cafés**, with a shorter indoor-leaning route.
- Transit suggestion: **JR train** is the cleanest option; use a short taxi if you want to reduce local walking.
- Estimated cost: Train, temple fees, lunch, snacks, and dinner: **$210 total**.

### Day 3: Museum Day and Central Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- Morning: Spend the first half at the **Kyoto National Museum** or another indoor museum of your choice.
- Afternoon: Walk a relaxed central route around **Nishiki Market** and nearby shopping streets.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: Walk a relaxed central route around **Nishiki Market** and nearby shopping streets, Kyoto, Japan
- Food: Make this your best local-food day with **market snacks, obanzai, tamagoyaki, and matcha**.
- Rainy-day backup: Keep the same plan; this is already your best weather-proof day.
- Transit suggestion: Use **subway** for the museum and market area; it minimizes transfers and keeps the day easy.
- Estimated cost: Museum admission, subway, lunch, snacks, and dinner: **$170 total**.

### Day 4: Quiet Northern Kyoto Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** early, then continue to a slower temple stop such as **Ryoan-ji**.
- Afternoon: Keep the pace light with a neighborhood café break and one more nearby temple or garden.
- Food: Choose a calm lunch of **udon, set meals, or seasonal Kyoto vegetables**.
- Rainy-day backup: Shift to **Daitoku-ji area** or a smaller indoor cultural stop, then shorten the temple loop.
- Transit suggestion: Use **bus + a taxi backup** for the least tiring movement between northern sites.
- Estimated cost: Transit, entries, lunch, snacks, and dinner: **$190 total**.

### Day 5: Fushimi Sake District and Easy Finish
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Head to **Fushimi Inari Taisha** early, but keep it to a partial climb so the day stays relaxed.
- Afternoon: Shift to the **Fushimi sake district** for a slower walk, tasting, or riverside time.
- Food: Try **sake-friendly izakaya dishes**, rice bowls, and a final Kyoto dessert stop.
- Rainy-day backup: Focus on the **sake museum / tasting side of Fushimi** and shorten the shrine walk.
- Transit suggestion: **JR + short walk** works well; a taxi is a good fallback after the shrine if energy is low.
- Estimated cost: Transit, shrine visit, lunch, tastings, and farewell dinner: **$160 total**.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

- Day 1: **$180**
- Day 2: **$210**
- Day 3: **$170**
- Day 4: **$190**
- Day 5: **$160**

Total estimated on-trip spend: **$910**

That leaves about **$890** from your **$1,800** budget for:
- nicer meals
- extra temple admissions
- taxis on tiring days
- souvenirs
- a room upgrade or flexible reserve
